claims.claim: Quintus Septimius Florens Tertullian was a Carthaginian Christian theologian and presbyter who lived circa 155–220 AD.
Tertullian wrote primarily in Latin and is considered the father of Latin Christianity.
He composed On the Veiling of Virgins (De virginibus velandis) probably around AD 204.
The treatise argues that Christian virgins should wear a head covering in church once they have passed puberty.
Tertullian addresses the work to unmarried women (virgins) and also appeals to married women in the Christian community of Carthage.
The work was written to counter a local custom in Carthage where some argued that virgins need not veil, presenting a controversy over head‑covering practice.
Tertullian bases his argument on Scripture (1 Cor 11) and on the principle that truth, not custom, should govern church discipline.
